title: Ida Jackson's house and his band
summary: Played many jobs at Ida Jackson's house with pianist Herbert Bloom, Albert Burbank and others, and heard Willie Jackson at Tom Anderson's.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Ida Jackson, did she have a house? Did she have one of the language ladies?
Yeah, she had a house and we used to play there. And our piano player was, his name was Herbert Bloom. He's in California right now. Good piano player.
No. Not the Bloom? Bloom, Herbert Bloom. Herbert Bloom. He was a good piano player.
Who else was in your band then that I didn't answer?
Oh, well Ida Jackson used to play with us too, Burbank. You know, Burbank.
Or Albert Burbank. Albert Burbank, yeah.

Well when he was, you know, didn't have a regular job, but whenever I wanted a client to play and couldn't get Pico, I'd get him. And then sometime I'd get this fellow, George, George Thomas, that's cornbread. Oh yeah, yeah. Brother Conrad. Brother Conrad, yeah. I'd get him. I'd get him to play and he'd play when we'd have a job or so. You know this fellow, Ida? Willie Jackson?
No, I never, a singer? Singer, yeah. New Orleans, they call it New Orleans Willie Jackson. Yeah, Willie Jackson.
He was singing at Tom Anderson's, right at Iberville and Ramport.
Did you ever work at Tom Anderson's too?

No, I never worked at Tom Anderson's, never did. Never did work at Tom Anderson's. But we used to see, when them times we used to go around and play, you know what I mean, for different people, you know. Yeah. And we used to go around and play just for fun, you know. I had the fellows that say, man let's go to my so and so's house today, you know. Pete would take his violin. I'd take my, I'd, sometime I'd take my banjo, sometime I'd tear the piano, I wouldn't take my banjo. I'd play the piano, you see what I mean?
